name: Dark Fiber — telecom overbuild (1996–2004) ↔ AI capex (2023–26)
positionLabel: Phase 6 of 8 · phase 7 beginning in two issuers (as of Aug 2026)

checklist.label: The catalyst makes capex non-optional
checklist.note: Entry condition is the removal of the option to abstain, not optimism. Tell: capex guidance revised upward in consecutive quarters without revised return assumptions.

checklist.label: The demand number becomes load-bearing
checklist.note: One unauditable extrapolation embedded simultaneously in equity model, bond covenant, capex plan. Tell: whether anyone starts disclosing utilisation (in telecom it arrived only after the defaults).

checklist.label: Self-funded expansion — the hedge phase
checklist.note: Early capacity genuinely scarce, early returns genuinely good; manufactures the evidence for later phases.

checklist.label: Migration into debt — the speculative phase
checklist.note: Capex outruns operating cash flow; the gap is bonded (capex/OCF → 100%). Tell: equity returning to the funding mix for former net buyers of their own stock.

checklist.label: Off-balance-sheet — reported numbers stop describing the economics
checklist.note: Obligations move where analysts can't size them; the loss lands in unexpected places. Tell: depreciation critique — the mitigant (earnings-led market) and the risk are the same number.

checklist.label: Vendor and circular finance — the Ponzi phase
checklist.note: Form matched, degree early. Supplier lends the customer the money to buy the supplier's product; a trap, not primarily a fraud. Tell: first material customer-receivable write-down at a vendor or GPU-collateralised lender.

checklist.label: The credit turn — which leads the equity turn
checklist.note: Beginning, idiosyncratic — two issuers. Credit priced the telecom collapse before equity, legibly and dateably. Tell: idiosyncratic → systemic — broad HY widening while issuer CDS keeps widening.

checklist.label: Liquidation, and the second act
checklist.note: Assets clear at salvage; the surplus is real but captured by users, not financiers. Sharpest AI divergence: 2–3y GPU life means stranded compute has no second act.

tripwires.label: Broad HY transmission
tripwires.threshold: HY OAS > 450bp while AI-issuer credit widens
tripwires.note: Live-wired to FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2. Baseline: HY OAS 271bps (2026-08-12) vs ~450bps long-run median — not fired as of this ledger.

tripwires.label: Vendor-financing impairment
tripwires.threshold: First AI-vendor receivable write-down or impairment disclosed (telecom precedent: Lucent/Nortel/Motorola bad-loan shares surged from single digits to 60–80% within a year)
tripwires.note: Manual watch — flip in themes.json when observed. Baseline: no AI-vendor receivable write-down through mid-Aug-2026; Nvidia's allowance is ~0.02% of AR (three customers = 30/18/16% of AR).

tripwires.label: Useful-life revisions
tripwires.threshold: A hyperscaler or AI-infra vendor revises server/GPU useful-life assumptions downward (the depreciation-understatement mechanism Burry alleges: ~$176bn 2026–28, Oracle ~26.9% / Meta ~20.8% overstated by 2028)
tripwires.note: Manual watch — flip in themes.json when observed. Burry's claim is contested by CoreWeave/Nvidia, not confirmed.

tripwires.label: Utilisation disclosure
tripwires.threshold: A major AI-infra operator discloses declining data-center/GPU utilisation (telecom precedent: fibre lit share only ~3.9% through Chicago per TeleGeography, ~2.7% in-use per WSJ, by 2002)
tripwires.note: Manual watch — flip in themes.json when observed. CoreWeave's ~95% re-lease rate on off-contract H100s is cited as current counter-evidence.

figures.text: Nvidia's Sept-2025 $100bn letter of intent to OpenAI was never consummated; replaced Feb-2026 by a $30bn equity stake in OpenAI's $110bn round plus binding 3GW inference / 2GW training hardware commitments.
Best-sourced sizing of the interlocking AI-compute web is >$750bn (Bloomberg, 2026-07-27), not the >$800bn figure in the original doc.

Alphabet priced an $84.75bn equity program (common stock + mandatory convertibles + a $40bn ATM + a $10bn Berkshire placement) in June 2026, with ~$49.6bn of cash actually received in Q2; it also issued a separate $20.3bn of senior notes — not a flat '$84.75bn raised.'
Alphabet's uncommenced-lease jump from $23.9bn to $42.6bn was Q2-2025 → Q3-2025, not a single quarter within 2026 as the original phrasing implied.
Amazon's $53.4bn Anthropic-stake gain is real but ran through non-operating income, not operating results (operating income was $27.5bn, +43%).

S&P Q2-26 EPS +50.4% headline vs +32.0% 'underlying' — FactSet's +32.0% figure is EPS growth excluding Alphabet and Amazon as companies, not an ex-one-offs adjustment; the substantive point (headline masks concentration) still holds.
The 2s10s Treasury spread re-steepened to ~+48–52bps by mid-Aug-2026, not the ~+35bps figure (which traces to a single secondary commentary source).
CoreWeave's rebuttal figure is a ~95% re-lease rate on off-contract H100/A100 GPUs (rebooked near the original rental rate), not '~95% resale values.'

Greenwood–Shleifer–You: run-up size alone (without added attributes) already spans a 20%→80% crash-odds range (50%→150% net-of-market gains); added attributes sharpen the estimate further. Run-up size still fails to predict low average returns going forward (Fama's point); the ~6-month-later peak and ~30% further gain after high-run-up-plus-attributes episodes is confirmed.
Telecom/communications was ~55% of defaulted high-yield dollars in 2001 and ~52% in 2002 (Altman, NYU Salomon Center 2002) — not the original doc's 'media+telecom 44% in 2001, 65% in 2002.'
$148bn of high-yield issuance was 1998 alone, not a 1997–98 average; 1997 issuance was ~$119bn (1997–98 average ~$133bn), and the 1995–96 average was ~$50bn (Altman/NYU series).

Cisco did vendor-finance in the telecom buildout (~$2.4bn committed, ≈30% of Lucent's $8.1bn; nine vendors totaled ~$25.6bn by end-2000) but carried no long-term debt — the accurate framing is 'limited vendor financing, no balance-sheet dependence,' not zero vendor-financing exposure.
Media+telecom = 45% / 57% of high-yield new issuance in 1999 / 2000 — traces only to an uncited Fabricated Knowledge blog post, the apparent origin of several telecom figures in the original doc.
~$800bn of telecom M&A in 1999 — plausible given known deals (Vodafone–Mannesmann ~$183bn, WorldCom–Sprint ~$129bn) but no primary source for the aggregate total was found.

Fibre ~10% lit by 2004 and wholesale long-haul prices −55% y/y in 2004 — unverified as stated. (The related <5%-lit-by-2002 claim IS confirmed: TeleGeography put 3.9% lit through Chicago and WSJ reported 2.7% in-use.)
Oracle 5Y CDS '~43bps mid-2025' — unverified as a precise print; use the sourced framing '<50bps pre-OpenAI-deal' instead.

S&P downgraded Oracle to BBB− on 2026-07-09 (negative free cash flow of roughly −$24bn FY26; OpenAI ≈ half of Oracle's $638bn RPO); Oracle's 5Y CDS hit a record ~203bps on 2026-07-24 and ~215bps by mid-Aug-2026.
CoreWeave's 5Y CDS trades near 855bps — roughly a 50% cumulative 5-year default probability at 40% recovery — alongside +125bps loan spreads and tightening covenant demands.
Broad high-yield OAS is 271bps (2026-08-12) vs a ~450bps long-run median; investment-grade OAS is ~81bps and EFFR is 3.63%.
Hyperscaler capex runs ≈94% of operating cash flow in 2026–27 (PIMCO/Epoch/FactSet).
Incremental debt as a share of capex rose 9%→32% from FY24 to the latest twelve months (FactSet).
Uncommenced hyperscaler leases: Moody's estimates $662bn (113% of adjusted debt); Goldman ~$1tn; Reuters' bottom-up estimate ~$1.09tn; Oracle alone ~$260bn.

Alphabet's Q2-2026 free cash flow was −$5.9bn, its first negative quarter since the 2004 IPO (trailing-twelve-month FCF still +$53.3bn); buybacks have been halted (Alphabet $13.2bn→$0, Meta $0 in Q1-26).

Michael Burry (Nov-2025) claims ~$176bn of understated AI-infrastructure depreciation over 2026–28, with Oracle ~26.9% and Meta ~20.8% of earnings overstated by 2028 — carried here as a claim, contested by CoreWeave and Nvidia, not an established fact.
No AI-vendor receivable write-down had occurred through mid-Aug-2026: Nvidia's allowance for doubtful accounts is ~0.02% of AR, with three customers concentrating 30%/18%/16% of AR.

Cecilia Wagner Ricci's (Montclair State) telecom bad-loan shares end-2000→end-2001 — Lucent 2.6%→60%, Nortel 25.5%→80%, Motorola 6.7%→57% — match Newsweek's 'The Stupid Loan Bubble' (2002-10-27) exactly.
Telecom high-yield spreads moved 2,100bps (Oct-2002) → 500bps (Jul-2004) (FRBSF Economic Letter 2004-32); roughly $2tn of telecom market value was destroyed over the bust.
